column1: # The in-guest Rust compiler (`rustc-root-x86` builds it, `just bootstrap` gave
# it a sysroot). Driven by `cargo xtask gate rustc`, on the disk image whose root
# is the same staged tree the C toolchain lives in.
# `/usr/bin/rustc` finds its sysroot in `<exe>/../..`, so `/usr/lib/rustlib/
# <triple>/lib` is where the rlibs were staged and no `--sysroot` is needed; that
# path comes from `dladdr`, which `minix-libc` answers from `/proc/self/exe`. The
# host triple compiled into the binary is the target triple, so a bare `rustc`
# already targets x86_64-pc-minix.
# `threadprobe` runs first because the compiler builds its session on a spawned
# thread: a thread-local block, an 8 MiB stack, heap allocation and a directory
# walk of the sysroot are what the compiler needs before it prints anything, and
# `threadtest` covers only `minix_rt::thread_create` itself.
# Three things are named on the compile line on purpose:
#   * `-C linker=/usr/bin/ld.lld`: the lld the toolchain gate already proved;
#   * `-T/usr/lib/minix-user.ld`: the image bases the spec's `--defsym` flags
#     expect, which a build script normally passes;
#   * `/usr/lib/libminix-libc.rlib`: `std`'s backtrace names `_Unwind_Backtrace`,
#     whose port stub is in the C library, and no Rust crate imports it.
# A `wc -c` follows the compile because an empty expectation also matches the
# blank line the console prints, so a compile that failed with diagnostics would
# otherwise still read as "ok".
/usr/bin/threadprobe
/usr/bin/rustc --version
/usr/bin/rustc -C linker=/usr/bin/ld.lld -C link-arg=-T/usr/lib/minix-user.ld -C link-arg=/usr/lib/libminix-libc.rlib -o /tmp/hello-rs /usr/src/hello.rs
/bin/coreutils wc -c /tmp/hello-rs
/tmp/hello-rs
